texto:
This week, control of both the House and the Senate changed hands in a single midterm election.

It sounds rare. It isn't.

In 2006, Democrats gained thirty-one House seats and six Senate seats, and took both chambers.

In 1994, it went the other way. Republicans gained fifty-four House seats and eight in the Senate, and won the House for the first time in forty years.

The pattern is old: the president's party almost always loses ground in a midterm. Since 1934, it has gained House seats only three times: 1934, 1998 and 2002.

The new Congress, with its new majorities, will be sworn in this January.

Different decades. Different parties. Same midterm pattern. The American File.
titulo: Congress just flipped. When did this last happen? #shorts
